target_year_over_year_context.explanation:

previous_disclosures.summary: Complex large language models (LLMs) and large vision models (LVMs) are disrupting traditional search and content creation methods by offering enhancements in consumer utility. Qualcomm believes innovative enterprise and consumer use cases will emerge as these models run on-device, leveraging multiple sensor modalities to provide immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure expands the technology scope by introducing 'small language models (SLMs)' and 'large multimodal models (LMMs)' alongside existing LLMs/LVMs. This reflects a meaningful evolution in the technical strategy and addressable market for Qualcomm's on-device AI capabilities, moving beyond just large models to include more tailored and multimodal approaches.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2024 disclosures cover the landscape of AI model investment (LLMs, SLMs, etc.), their disruption of user experiences, and the strategic view that these models must run on-device for privacy and utility. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) covers the exact same specific points: the development of LLMs/SLMs/LVMs/LMMs, their disruption of search/content, and the necessity of on-device execution for utility, privacy, and security. qcom_2024_1_D011 maps to the model landscape/disruption, and qcom_2024_1_D012 maps to the on-device necessity/utility argument found in qcom_2025_1_D010.

The 2024 disclosure expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities and increased adoption. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) contains the specific sentence: 'We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.' This is a direct textual and topical match.

previous_disclosures.summary: The market sees significant investment in LLMs, SLMs, LVMs, and LMMs for text, image, and multimodal applications, which are disrupting traditional search and content creation methods.
Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
Qualcomm expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities, with analysts estimating 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024.

current_disclosures.summary: Significant investment continues in developing various AI models (LLMs, SLMs, LVMs, LMMs) that disrupt traditional user experiences. While developed primarily for the cloud, these models must run on-device to maximize utility, privacy, and security, and the company expects continued advancement and adoption of generative AI capabilities in edge devices.

peer_results.rationale: Candidates focus on ROCm software ecosystem optimizations for training/inference workloads and professional GPU graphics features, which do not share the same specific topic of on-device AI utility drivers (privacy, immediacy, local inference benefits) as the target disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO address the specific utility of on-device or private generative AI by highlighting privacy and security as key benefits, though they operate in different sectors. QCOM emphasizes that AI must run on-device to maximize utility through immediacy and privacy, while AVGO’s VMware Private AI solution specifically enables organizations to use generative AI while addressing data privacy and compliance needs in a corporate context.

sentences.text: While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
• Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: While QCOM focuses specifically on the imperative of on-device generative AI for utility, INT broader strategic vision includes bringing AI to where data is generated and used, explicitly mentioning AI PCs and AI at the edge alongside cloud generative AI. Both recognize the significance of edge/on-device compute in the AI continuum, but QCOM frames it as a necessity for maximizing utility, whereas INT frames it as part of addressing every phase of the AI continuum.

sentences.text: While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.
Our strategy is to bring AI to where the data is being generated and used.

peer_results.rationale: Candidates discuss hardware innovations (DDR5, SSDs) to address memory bandwidth and storage demands for generative AI, which is a supporting infrastructure topic rather than the strategic or utility-focused discussion of on-device AI execution found in the target.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gamers and creators use NVIDIA GPUs for immersive experiences and content creation. The advent of generative AI is expected to drive broader adoption among PC users for local AI applications due to privacy, latency, and cost benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA identify privacy, latency, and cost as primary drivers for running generative AI applications locally (on-device) rather than solely in the cloud. QCOM argues on-device execution is necessary for these benefits, while NVDA notes that generative AI is expected to drive broader adoption of local PC GPUs for the same reasons: privacy, latency, and cost sensitivity.

sentences.text: While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.

With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.
